verdict.tagline: Deep combat and massive monsters trapped behind heavy technical friction.
for_you_if: you can overlook a weak story
you plan to play for a long time
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates in cities
you cannot accept a single save file
you want a bug-free startup experience

distortion_flags.sentence: Approval rates rise sharply the longer players stay with the game.

claims.claim: The game suffers from performance drops and frame rate issues, particularly in crowded areas or cities.

citations.review_text:
Having played Dragon's Dogma 2 at release on PS5 i really enjoyed my time with, but since there were no news about upcoming expansions i ended up stopping playing.

When i heard about the expansion i didn't mind getting the game again on computer since i play mostly on it.

Speaking about optimization issues that i had, i first thought it was no big deal some fps drops here and there didn't even notice them most of the time, but after i went to a different region i did notice a lot more frame drops than usual, while it didn't really affect me i do understand why people talk about it.

Just like at DD1 release, DD2 felt rushed, while in some areas its definetly superior to DD1 in others i feel its lacking, especially since the world is much bigger and the lack of variety of enemies starts to get noticeable, etc...

But even with its flaws i think its a gem of a game, rough around the edges but if it was given the time it needed it could be so much more... hopefully the dlc will fix some of the issues at hand.

Dragon's Dogma 2 is extremely fun, and I'm happy that the game is able to run on the Legion Go S Z2. However, there are extremely a lot of overwhelming performance issues. The game cannot even hold a solid 30 frames per second. The game is extremely taxing on my Legion Go S Z2, because even when the game is plugged into the wall, I'm only able to get six hours of gameplay, showing me signs that the gaming device is doing all that it can to run this game. I have never seen a more demanding game than Dragon's Dogma 2 on the Legion Go SZ2. Not even The Witcher 3 comes close to these frustrating performance issues. Other than that, the story is decent, adventuring is fun, and the combat is excellent. The performance issues are holding this game back from getting into the hands of many more people. For people who own gaming handhelds, we should be able to enjoy this game similar to console players.

Played on MSI CLAW ULTRA 7

I have this game on my Series X and it was super fun. Bought the PC version because I want to play this handheld unfortunately the experience wasn't good. I grew up with consoles so 30FPS or lower doesn't bother me but man, the crashes killed the fun.

"Its an handheld no duh crashes are abound"
Sure, but the game ran relatively OK. Outside of Vernmouth no problem. I can explore to my heart content without worries of the game crashing but inside of the city is where the fun dies. Changing Vocation or opening Buy will crash the game (oddly enough switching controls to Desktop Mode mitigated the crashing) and walking in the city WILL crash the game. I doubt Capcom will fix this but if you are planning on playing this game on handheld, do be wary before making the purchase. If you have a PC or consoles, play DD2 there and safe yourself from a heartbreak.

The game is amazing.

Everywhere you go, anything you try to do, you will see something new.
The open world is very well realized, there's always secrets and fun to discover in it.

The combat is really good, the classes are unique, and overall it truly feels like going on an epic journey.


It launched in a terrible state two years ago, with horrible performance and lots of bugs and mechanics that were very tedious.
Capcom has adressed virtually every single issue with two major free updates, full of quality of life, reworks and performance improvements. These are BEFORE the DLC expansion.

Regarding performance, it has been solid, except for the main city because each exit point loads in "the open world" (the game has no load times), so you will encounter more stutters there. That being said, the stutters are swift and not as annoying as they used to be.

In the open world, you will sometimes encounter a tiny stutter, but they are spread out decently and are also very swift, so they have not bothered me, as someone who can not stand stutters in general. 

I have not experienced any framedrops and cpu/gpu usage has been consistent.

I highly recommend the game if you are looking for an adventure that rewards curiosity and exploration.

I will also mention that the narrative is on the light side, but it is there. It's told more like a fairy tale, where things are basic but still epic. It is definitely not an "RPG" narrative, but I find it very effective for what the game is.

The character creator is very impressive.

Dragon Dogma II the trojan horse...

Adventure !!! Romance !!! Excitement !!! All of this while your PC fans are spinning like a helicopter...
Nothing better than to raise an enemy difficulty than to clock your GPU to 100%...

The devs had an amazing idea... Making your CPU spin its fans so fast in the cities, gives the game a more realistic felling, and the experience is much more engaging and dangerous... you never know when your PC will explode...

This devs are geniuses...  Who would ve thought  that the only thing you would had to do to buff the enemies difficulty would be to scare the player by spinning the PC fans when a big monster shows up, ITS SPECIAL EFFECTS IN REAL TIME not even VR can achieve this level of realism... I mean and not even horror games produce this kind of fear... Absolutely genius... this Devs are geniuses...

Next time you guys wanna sell a game just stick a grenade in the box... The user buys your game gives you a lot of $$$$,  kisses and good comments, then he opens the box and explodes, BUMMM, like the tricks those clowns do in the circus... That should give you dum dums a good laugh !!!

Played a lot on my PS5 and it's awesome game but still horribly optimized. I don't have the best hardware but ultra low or max settings make 0 difference to my fps it's just stuck at 40. Game uses 40% of my gpu and my CPU is just tapped out in the high 90s.

I recommend looking into Lossless Scaling on steam, the difference it will on this game is huge. For linux there is a github repo that will allow you to run it.

claims.claim: Players encounter game-breaking or annoying bugs involving NPC aggression and jail mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Wow what a shame, I loved the first Dragons Dogma and waited a long time to play this version after I saw the negative reviews.  I got to about 10 hours in, level 15 and I was enjoying myself but the bugs have beaten me.

There's a jail break quest that has caused a guard aggro bug that follows you across your save file and you cant get rid of without a long winded work around killing all your pawns, removing all your gear and sleeping on a bench 14 times in a far away land.  Having done that once, and had a few hours of disrupted gameplay trying to fix it, the aggro bug happened again back in the jail!

If that wasnt enough to cause me to quit, Ive just tried the reload from the last rest inn rest point.   But unknown to me, its not included rests at camps, so its wiped the last 8 hours of gameplay and put me back to level 2, so thats it, im done!  Gamebreaking bug!

I loved the first entry, it was a blast to play. This title has too many issues to even consider playing, and the real issue is that you won't see/experience the constant issues until about the 3 hour mark when you are frequenting populated areas. I have, in 3 separate inns, replicated a bug that causes the entire town of NPCs to aggro you after resting. Before resting, no agro, after resting, complete agro. You can also force NPCs in a town to agro by walking through doorways at a bad angle. You can also force NPCs to agro by CONSUMING A HEAL IN FRONT OF THEM. Ridiculous, CAPCOM, ridiculous.

claims.claim: The game features deep character customization and physics-based combat mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Dragons dogma is a cult classic. The combat has immense depth and the animations and movement feel vastly improved to the original. It has one of the deepest character customisation features in any game around and its enviroment and ambient music are so soothing and relaxing.

However, I would strongly reccomend using a mouse with multiple buttons as unfortunatly the control scheme is designed with consoles in mind. There are mods available to change the key binding issues but if you can tweak it and get used to it, its not as bad as people say. ( or just use a controller I guess)

Its not for everyone, its not a mainstream RPG, It has quirks and oddities. These only add to the immense charm of the game and once you click with it, youll see why so many people staunchly defend it as a fantastic RPG title.

I love this friggen game. So many people are bleh/hate it and compare to the first one. I must admit I didn't finish the first Dragon's Dogma Dark Arisen yet but I still prefer this one more... might be recency bias. This is my second and a half playthrough as the first was on PS5. My pc at the time was taking a number two so I waited a while before I built a new one.  Luckily they optimized this software better for PS5 back in the day but as of now it seems better for PC than it used to be. No slowdowns in town YET.

Sure the story of this game is no David Lynch's Eraserhead but its fine... that isn't what I came for. I came for the awesome character creator, adventure and observation of how my online friend's pawns are built. Some randos have interesting pawns as well. 

The animations in this game are amazing with little details and I guess they should be since its Capcom we're talking here. I enjoy them more than Monster Hunter's animations though those might be better games all in all I haven't played enough of them yet.

Every npc and character in this game's lip syncing is atrocious. Probably the worst I've seen in a while and you kind of want it to be good because many of the visuals are stunning. It's not as off putting when a game is deliberately goofy and has wonky lip sync but in this case its a bit uncalled for. But one of my favorite games is Elden Ring and they barely had lip sync so I guess I can't complain too much. 

The pawns can be SUPER annoying eventually so what I did is just disable all subtitles and turn the pawn voice slider way down. I didn't want it completely silent as it looks weird when their mouth is moving sometimes while all other npcs can talk just fine. I WISH the devs would make a toggleable option to have the pawns speak LESS not just make me turn their voices down all the way. They can be super annoying with their voices and the repetition of it eventually. Maybe there is a mod for that idk haven't checked for that specifically…

citations.review_text:
Playing this I remembered why I stopped buying AAA titles.
Whole thing feels vibe coded, NPCs popping in and out of existence, same lines spoken by pawns every few minutes, awful quests and story, and the main quest was obviously changed after launch because it was broken or provided too much friction, supposedly you have to wear noble garments (which you obtain on 3 separate occasions and more are stored along the way) to access court, it's no longer the case, you can stroll around butt naked no worries there. you can use your weapon to strike or punch any npc anywhere, no reaction, but if you walk with weapon drawn other npcs will be "alert" and will also draw their weapon, you can then smack them, no issue, won't react
gear progress is a joke, to get better gear you use your gold to buy weapons from stores; which obviously makes loot and looting pointless, you open chest you get a potion, which you won't ever need because in your party mage just casually aoe heals everyone as many times as you'd like
there are so many things broken in this game that I 100% know that nobody that reviewed it played more than few hours, was a paid off reviewer or just simply completely braindead
it's dragon age but worse, and witcher without good combat, interesting monster lore and good loot
there's also no dodge button so if you're playing any class without built in mobility you can't fight without your pawns as you will get staggered from one hit
this game is sooo bad, I'd ashamed to sell it

How can this be worse than the first game?

It's ugly dirty brown and murky, what's the point of putting in RTX features that make my PC fans go into hoover mode for a game that looks this bad

Pawns. Constant repeating the same junk over and over in cringy fake fantasy thee and thou language.  Cringe

It's got amateur hour all over it.

Replay the first before you touch this junk

claims.claim: Reviewers report that quest directions and instructions can be vague, lacking clear guidance or map markers.

citations.review_text:
👍 20 hours in 2 days. That should tell you something.
The game itself is good, but there are several huge issues that seriously hurt the experience.

# Cons
### 1. Quests are terrible

They're not just poorly designed, they're often impossible to figure out without guides.

Half the time the game gives you almost no information. Your quest hint might literally be something like:

> "Go east."

That's it.

You'll spend an hour talking to every NPC, running in circles, searching every cave because the game refuses to tell you anything useful. Markers? Nope.

I spent **3 hours** looking for one cave only to find out the NPC had already been torn apart by wolves before I arrived, so I got almost no reward.

Thanks, Capcom.

Another quest gave me actual PTSD.

To progress, I had to talk to **children**. The game never tells you that. It doesn't even tell you that you need to talk to anyone. Since 99% of NPCs are just decoration, I spent forever checking half the city, talking to everyone, even jumping off cliffs just in case. Eventually I randomly found a little girl near a well.

Only then did the main quest continue.

And yes, this quest is mandatory.

---

### 2. Way too much pointless traveling

Many quests send you across the entire map for no good reason.

Then the game throws scripted obstacles at you - a broken bridge, for example - turning a 20-minute run into a 30-minute run.

It's not challenging. It's just wasting your time.

---

### 2.5 Ox carts

Great idea.

Watching the scenery while the ox does the work sounds relaxing.

Except the ox moves at about **2 km/h**, and it's literally several times slower than simply running yourself. You can skip tho...

---

### 3. Inventory is a mess

You have like 15 different healing items, all taking separate inventory slots.

Then food does basically the same thing.

Half your carry weight ends up being medicine and groceries.

---

### 4. Barely any RPG choic…

My game crashed after serveral hours of playing, which was frustrating. I also wanted to play as a Warrior from the start, but the game locked the class behide a quest that wasn't clearly explained. I found a great sword, brought a staff, and still had to figure out on my own that I specifically needed archistaff. The quest instructions are too vague and left me confuse instead of immersed. That said I really liked the graphics, character creation, combat and overall art style. My biggest complaint is that the game gets in the way of letting you play a class you actually wanted. and the quest are long and boring. I would give this game a 4/10

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the story as bland, uninteresting, and underwhelming.

citations.review_text: The combat in this game is genuinely amazing! However story is bland and uninteresting, also world feels empty and enemy variety is lackluster
Dragons Dogma is an acquired taste its punishing but not unfair while the story was under whelming it's the adventure that counts with these games and what an amazing adventure it is

Gotta say that was a living hell of an experience.

While I liked character creator and the battle mechanics, the story was underwhelming. This game is all about grinding and upgrading your stuff and makes very little effort to connect you with the world and characters.

Not to mention the absolute lackluster of the gameplay design and user interface. It takes serious googling to figure out a lot of things that should help you simply progress in the game because it is so unintuitive. And in the Unmoored, one second you get distracted and wont revive yourself with a stone, it is a game over and start anew. Which is so wild to me to get punished like that and not being able to save or anything.

Which again, is just a pointless sequence of battles with no real deep story attached (just beat a BBEG and become the ruler) and no real "motivation" to start over.


I barely figured out how to get the Unmoored ending, and there as soon as I died once and I lost all desire to play because there is nothing in it for me, and there is no connection to characters or world developed to want to actually save it. 

Those who like grinding gear, and tediousness of constant battles, just for the sake of battles, is a good game. For those who likes the story and meaning behind everything, I would recommend to skip this one.

As I bought it with DLC I might try it gain with DLC just out of curiosity but I doubt I will change my opinion because the core aspects are a "no" from me.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game has a limited and repetitive variety of normal enemies and monsters.

citations.review_text: The combat in this game is genuinely amazing! However story is bland and uninteresting, also world feels empty and enemy variety is lackluster

This game is perfection and bad at the same time. I'd absolutely recommend to get it if you liked DDDA, Skyrim, or even Elden Ring. 
Pros:
-combat
-exploration
-area design
-art design
-soundtrack
-immersion
-drip
-pawn system
-vocations
-One of the best end game experiences I've ever had in a game
-towns and Npcs
-tons of quest
-fast travel implementation balances convenience and encouragement to explore


CONS
-[u] EXTREME lack of enemy variety [/u] (by far the absolute worst  thing about this game)
-[u] Enemy Ai [/u] in this game can range from full on stagger locking you to death perfectly to literally being lobotomized and can not get over a rock or by a tree
-[u] Barely any weapon or gear progression early on [/u](you will get consumables 99% of the time from chest that require you to pathfind to them and parkore or complete an entire dungeon)
-[u] One save file [/u](The dlc patch is going to fix this)
-[u] NG+ does NOT scale enemies up [/u] so it feels braindead and is essentially only there in case you missed the true ending or other quest. imo combined with the lack of enemies this really kills the replayabilty of the game
-[u] soundtrack [/u](yes it is good, but it is simultaneously a failure. DD and DDDA's ost were so far and above better than DD2's ost that it is genuinely embarassing and a shame to even share a title with them)

Game looks very good and runs well, the combat system is alright and slaying big monsters is super satisfying. Howerver, there are some very annoying issues with the game that make me regret playing it every time I pick it back up. 
For one: It's annoying how constant the fights are, especially with how limited the trash mob variety is. Literally can't run anywhere without a fight every 15 seconds. I'd like to be able to explore and sight see, but I pause for a second and it's -Boom goblins run up behind you, or harpies shrieking incessantly. It's especially heinous in escort missions where you can't just run through the mobs. You may think I'm exaggerating, but I ♥♥♥♥ you not, on one escort in the span of one minute I ran into 5 different mobs of enemies and had to carry this elven turd through each of them because he would go out of his way to fight every one.

Dragon’s Dogma 2 was a massive disappointment after the first game. I waited twelve years for a proper sequel that would build on what made the original special, fix its obvious problems, and finally realize its wasted potential. Instead, it often feels like a prettier remake carrying many of the exact same issues.

Is this seriously the game I waited twelve years for? The combat is better, the world is larger, and the presentation is more modern, but rather than moving the formula forward, Dragon’s Dogma 2 mostly recreates it, including limitations that should have been left behind over a decade ago.

The combat is still genuinely incredible. Climbing onto huge monsters, attacking weak points, and taking advantage of the chaos created by the physics system is easily the best part. Monsters can fall off cliffs, destroy bridges, crash into each other, or turn a normal journey into a massive battle. The vocations are just as strong. They completely change how you play, and trying new skills and weapons carried a huge part of the game for me.

The Pawn system is still one of the most unique ideas in gaming. Hiring other players’ Pawns, having them guide you through quests they know, and listening to them during long journeys makes the world feel alive. They can be repetitive and incredibly stupid, but they are still a major part of what makes Dragon’s Dogma feel unlike anything else.

The world also looks great. Its environments, lighting, effects, and large-scale fights can be genuinely impressive. Exploring is exciting at first because the world feels dangerous and unpredictable.

The problem is that the further I got, the more unfinished the game felt.

The story sets up a political conflict involving Disa and the False Sovran, makes reclaiming the throne seem like the central plot, and then almost completely abandons it. Even the Dragon barely matters in a game called Dragon’s Dogma. Just when it finally felt like the real story was about to begin, the game rushed …

TL;DR: A more refined version of DD1, definitely worth on sale for any RPG fan.

[h2] The good [/h2]
[list]
 [*] you can freely switch between classes, and unlock all the skills. Every class is different, you can often change your playstyle if you get bored.
 [*] a lot of stuff to find in the open world. For the masochists (like me), all the seeker tokens.
 [*] bossfights are cool early in the game when you can't one shot boss with 8 health bars with a single ability.
 [*] overall, a more improved and refined version of DD1.
[/list]

[h2] The bad[/h2]
[list]
 [*] Combat can get stale if you keep the same class.
 [*] Pawn AI is kinda stupid
 [*] controls on keyboard are.. meh. I can clearly see the game was made primarily for controllers.
 [*] I would welcome dodge for all classes, not only thief. With that being said, I can understand why it is only for specific class, so just my preference I suppose.
 [*] Class balancing is a bit off
 [*] Enemy variety is... limited
 [*] Optimization is kind of meh, was getting between 30-50 FPS depending on location on high settings, you can see my specs thanks to steam's useful feature.
[*] no real romance option. You can raise NPC affinity, they will blush, but nothing changes except for slightly different dialog.
[/list]

So overall, despite the game having it's issues, it was quite enjoyable 78 hours I spent, worth the price on sale.

Don't play DD2 as though it's any other action RPG. It's committed to ambience, emergent gameplay, and a living world more so than the typical RPG and it gives up some things you'd expect in other entries like skyrim for example. I won't say that it totally hits the mark. Often times certain aspects will feel somewhat tedious or half baked. There's a lot of walking for instance. Though the obfuscation of certain mechanics goes a long way towards enhancing the sense of a unique world to learn and understand it also can be very frustrating and lead to a pervasive anxiety about missing things or failing quests. I'd recommend it as a fairly unique experience though I'd definitely get it on sale if you aren't familiar with the first game already and know what you're getting in to. Combat can take a while to click and because of the structure of the game it will likely take more than 2 hours to get comfortable with it. 

There have been a number of complaints about performance but there's a wide range of settings to make the game plenty playable with certain settings having a massive effect on their own. Still it's likely to chug on lower end PC's unless you bump down the resolution. Out in the open where you'll spend the vast majority of the game it runs well for me with few if any major fps spikes. It chugs in cities but that isn't a deal breaker for me as you don't typically do much combat there.

I have a Ryzen 9 7945HX and 4070 mobile, and the game runs great once I figured out how to make it work.

1 - It took me about 3 to 4 days to finally understand how the settings impact game performance. For example, as soon as you load the game in the city the VRAM spikes up, and after a few minutes it goes 
down.

2 - In any case, I try to lower the textures from 2GB to 1GB inside the big city and the VRAM is not a 
problem.

3 - The FPS is low by nature inside the city, like 55 at best and 45 here and there, but it’s playable I guess.

4 - Took me 3 hours of tinkering with the settings to fix the shadows in the trees flickering problem by reducing shadow from max to high.

5 - For VRAM, I turned off frame generation and I am all good. Since most of the game is played outside the cities, I get a good 65 to 75 FPS consistent outdoors and the VRAM stays around 6.5GB.

Dragon's Dogma 2 is a difficult game to review because, despite all of its flaws, I still had a great time with it. I enjoyed it so much that I completed 100% of the game, but at the same time I cannot ignore the feeling that this was supposed to be a bigger evolution of the original.

My experience with the game started with a lot of frustration. At launch, Dragon's Dogma 2 had serious performance problems. With a Ryzen 3600 and RTX 4070 Ti, I could barely maintain around 30 FPS when entering larger cities. I had to use mods to force better performance and make the game run in a more acceptable way. Thankfully, many of these issues have been improved over time, and the current version is much better than the launch release.

The biggest strength of Dragon's Dogma 2 is that it still feels like Dragon's Dogma. The atmosphere, world design and unique approach to fantasy RPGs are still here. The game has a special charm that separates it from other titles in the genre. Exploring the world, fighting monsters and traveling with your pawns still creates moments that few other RPGs can replicate.

The combat is still fun, but this is also where one of my biggest disappointments comes from. The first game had an incredible combat system with different classes that completely changed how you played. Dragon's Dogma 2 improves the presentation but does not push the system far enough. In many ways, combat feels like a step sideways rather than a true evolution, and some aspects are actually less satisfying than in the original.

The story is another mixed element. While the game has a fantastic twist but the overall storytelling is weaker than the first game. The way the plot is presented and how some events are handled leaves a lot to be desired.

Unfortunately, Dragon's Dogma 2 repeats some of the mistakes of the original instead of fixing them. The game takes several big steps forward, but also takes smaller steps backward in areas where fans expected improvements.

citations.review_text:
I originally bought Dragon’s Dogma 2 at launch and never really got into it. The vocation system felt unappealing at first, and systems like resting at an inn came across more as annoyances than meaningful mechanics. Years later, after hearing about the upcoming DLC, I returned to the game and this time the experience was completely different. 

The latest patches (including items like the Eternal Ferrystone) make a noticeable improvement to quality of life, but the original game itself is special. Even after 130 hours, I’m still planning to dive back in for the DLC. 

The vocation system is the real star. I didn't get it the first time, yet on this playthrough it completely won me over. Vocations I had zero interest in trying ended up being some of the most enjoyable once I gave them a proper chance. Every class has its own distinct feel and strengths, and that variety keeps the game fresh.

The world and environment are excellently crafted. Exploring the world often reminded me of Death Stranding, the same sense of quiet wonder, of looking at a distant ridge or ruin and thinking “I wonder if I can actually get up there.” The world feels large and rewarding to explore, and the environmental challenges (terrain, weather, resource management) make traversal feel purposeful rather than just a means of getting from A to B.

Combat benefits hugely from the vocation system. Sticking to one class for too long can grow repetitive, but the freedom to switch (and the distinct playstyles each vocation offers) keeps fights engaging. Boss and large monster encounters deliver some genuinely memorable moments, climbing, staggering, and coordinating with pawns creates those classic Dragon’s Dogma set pieces. 

That said, the roster of enemies does start to feel familiar after a while. More variety in the bestiary would have gone a long way toward keeping the combat high points feeling fresh throughout a long playthrough.

The narrative itself is fairly average for most of the runt…

I write this review in hopes that anyone debating on playing it before or after the dlc drops in October. Dragon's Dogma 2 is honestly quite phenomenal. The game itself is a marvel in just near every way. The combat is amazing, it has always been one of the best selling points in the series. The story is alright, but really the side content in the game is really what gets the core of the experience. 

The story really feels like it's happening at every moment when you're immersed in it. The way the companions, the pawns, feel as you work and fight together really makes the adventure feel alive. The classes, the vocations, are all varied yet enjoyable all the same. Its both a game you could huddle in a deep wiki read or play entirely on your own and make it the whole way through. 

Character progression feels really nice for bulk of the game. Near the end it starts to scale worse, with the player being way too powerful, but at the same time it feels organic for who is a living legend. The story of Dragons Dogma 1 isn't attached to this game either, so you won't miss anything if you start here, but really you should play it, it's so good.

This game is one of the only games I could ever deem worth the price, the whole game feels so alive, traveling feels good both on cart, on foot, or fast travel with the teleport stones. My first playthrough was over 100 hours, my second playthrough has reached 60 hours as of now, and I've still so much left to do. If you enjoy action jrpg's this is it. This is thE jrpg.

No microtransactions that you need to do good. Any that exist still are redundant and easily acquired on your own. No enemy feels out of place, traveling feels real, resting feels respiteful, winning tough battles is rewarding, and leveling up your class or character truly feels just right.

Combat is phenomenal. Watching your companion pick up combat cues from your gameplay was a blast to watch, and the vocations are all diverse and unique, despite it's extremely generic Tolkein-inspired fantasy.

Following the model of "show not tell" quests range from "move from A to B" to having to solve a quest with nothing more than a general message from your journal, leaving the rest to you.

Overall, try it. You'll find out if you're gonna like the game before the refund window closes.

At the time of this review, I've decided to replay the game again in prep for the dlc and the DD2gether mod coming out soon. I started maybe a few months ago, but I've been locked into a chokehold by the game and I can't play anything else. I really enjoy the combat. I also get to basically play fantasy dress up with me and my finace while she absolutely murderizes everything in the area and basically picks every flower and rock she can find (some how the pawn A.I. knows her). I'm really excited to see what the dlc brings in a few month. All of the vocations feel different by a bit and you can see which is supposed to be what "role" by the abilities, but any vocation is capable of doing anything. Def can sink some hours into the game and have fun while you do. I mean, Mystic Spearhand has a "Yeet" ability where you can send goblins to the moon. What's not to love?

Pros:
- Pawn system is unique and extremely fun
- Vocation depth and variety is excellent
- Environment looks fantastic and is exciting to explore
- Combat system is fun and highly satisfying

Cons:
- Game constantly crashes, PC performance is brutal, required to play on lowest graphics
- Not many quests, main story too short
- Story is alright, nothing too memorable

Overall: (7/10) The game is fun but falls short of it's full potential. Needs better PC optimisation.
